content:
maria: heads-up — ran the hetero quant + batching sweep this morning, and saw a reproducible accuracy delta when prefix cache is enabled vs disabled. putting raw numbers below.

vijay: can you paste the exact config you used? which models/quant libs (awq/gptq/fp8/int8)? :thinking:

maria: experiment matrix: AWQ-int8 gptq-int8 fp8-hybrid across two runtime pins (v1.21 optimized kernels, v1.22 fallback). Batch horizon set to 40ms continuous batching, prefix cache enabled with TTL=300s. eval set = 50k prompts (mix of chat and long-context QA).

sam: notable logs from the failing run:
```
[2026-03-18 03:12:07] batcher: formed batch size=8 latency=22ms
[2026-03-18 03:12:07] kvcache: hit_prefix=0.62 miss=0.38
[2026-03-18 03:12:08] model[awq-int8]: quant-round-mode=per-tensor
[2026-03-18 03:12:08] model[awq-int8]: kv-state-encoding=compact
[2026-03-18 03:12:09] eval: rougeL_drop=1.9% (baseline 0.5%)
```
looks like rouge/L and exact-match delta correlate with kvcache hit-rate swings.

jen: is this only when batching horizon > X? or any continuous batching?

maria: we tried no-batching (direct passthrough), small-batches (horizon=10ms) and current 40ms. deltas: no-batch: +0.2% rougeL over baseline; 10ms: +0.6%; 40ms: +1.9%. So worse with larger continuous batches.

vijay: hypothesis: quantized models (esp AWQ per-tensor scales) are sensitive to KV cache reuse because cached activations were computed under different numeric rounding contexts (batch boundary affects fused-kernel ordering). KV reuse means subsequent tokens see slightly different quant error distribution. Over long prefixes the drift accumulates and quality regresses.

kai: another angle — heterogeneous model variants: we fallback to fp8-variant for cold start, then switch to awq-int8 once warmed. If prefix cache contains fp8-computed KV and we later serve with int8 weights, mismatch could definitely introduce artifacts. we should tag cache entries with "model-quant-tag" and invalidate on model-variant switch.

sam: added a minimal repro harness: run single convo where we switch quant variant mid-way and compare logits. script:
```
# pseudo
client.start(convo)
client.send(prefix)
client.flush()
warm_to_variant('awq-int8')
client.send(continuation)
compare_logits()
```
Observed KL divergence spikes right after variant switch when cache kept.

jen: CI bot ran the nightly eval group on the AWQ sweep earlier — any overlap?

ci-bot: nightly-eval: awq-int8 sweep completed. Key metric anomalies: rougeL delta +1.7% (regression), hallucination-rate +0.9%. Artifacts logged under run 2026-03-18-AWQ-1988.

maria: proposed mitigations: 1) tag cache entries with quant variant + kernel-version, and invalidate on mismatch. 2) short TTL for prefix cache when hetero-variant rollouts are in progress. 3) add per-request header `x-quant-tag` so routing keeps like-for-like. 4) experiment with `quant-aware-batcher` which pins quant context for a whole batch (force consistent kernel selection/order).

vijay: also consider warmup policy: when switching variants, do a small deterministic warmup (n=2 tokens) to prime KV in target quantization before serving user continuation. cheaper than full invalidation and might cut delta.

kai: ops/infra note — invalidating entire prefix cache will blow throughput for a bit. recommend a lazy-invalidate flow: mark mismatched entries stale and only recompute on next real request (while returning a fallback low-latency variant).

maria: actionable items:
- @sam to add quant-tag to kvcache proto and gate invalidation logic (sam assigned)
- @vijay to run controlled warmup microbenchmarks across awq/gptq/fp8 variants (vijay assigned)
- @jen to add monitoring for `kv-quant-mismatch` and `per-token-kl` spikes in console (jen assigned)

sam: started a small branch, config snippet:
```
kvcache:
  encode: compact
  tag_headers: [model_version, quant_variant, kernel_hash]
  stale_policy: lazy_invalidate
batcher:
  quant_consistency: true
  max_horizon_ms: 25
```
pushing PR in ~2h.

jen: SGTM. We'll put a canary rollout on dedicated pool first. add rollback if rougeL delta > 1%.

maria: thanks all. I'll collect the experiment logs into the onboarding doc and flag for the new model bring-up checklist (quant-aware caching step). :thumbsup:

kai: +1 — good catch. this was a subtle production-risk.

maria: end.
